answer: Because the signal calculation reruns each epoch, the forge weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the spiral settlement publishes the resulting shares. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 39% independent neighbours on the funding graph. A tight ring of 156 clones as a result holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 31 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
